question: How does the Transformer decoder differ from the encoder, and where do the queries, keys and values of the encoder-decoder attention come from?
final_text: I couldn't find this in the passages I retrieved from the three papers, so I won't guess. I searched: AIAYN §3.2.3 Applications of Attention in our Model; AIAYN §3 Model Architecture; AIAYN §3.1 Encoder and Decoder Stacks; AIAYN §3.3 Position-wise Feed-Forward Networks.

drafts: The decoder stack adds a third sub‑layer that performs multi‑head attention over the encoder’s output, whereas the encoder stack contains only self‑attention sub‑layers that attend to its own previous layer outputs [AIAYN:3.1:c009][AIAYN:3.2.3:c016]. In the encoder‑decoder attention, the queries are taken from the preceding decoder layer, while the keys and values are taken from the encoder’s output representations [AIAYN:3.2.3:c016]. The decoder also masks its self‑attention to prevent positions from attending to subsequent positions, preserving the auto‑regressive property [AIAYN:3.2.3:c016][AIAYN:3.1:c009]. The encoder’s self‑attention uses the same source for queries, keys, and values—the output of its previous encoder layer [AIAYN:3.2.3:c016]. The retrieved passages do not state any additional architectural differences beyond these points.

The decoder stack includes an additional sub‑layer that performs multi‑head attention over the encoder’s output, while the encoder stack consists only of self‑attention sub‑layers [AIAYN:3.1:c009]. In encoder‑decoder attention the queries come from the previous decoder layer and the keys and values come from the encoder’s output [AIAYN:3.2.3:c016]. Self‑attention in the encoder uses the same source for queries, keys and values—the output of the previous encoder layer [AIAYN:3.2.3:c016]. In the decoder, self‑attention is masked to prevent positions from attending to subsequent positions, preserving the auto‑regressive property [AIAYN:3.2.3:c016]. The retrieved passages do not state any further differences between encoder and decoder.
